## Natural history notes

A medium-sized owlet moth characterized by warm orange-brown to rusty forewings with darker wavy lines and mottled markings that help it blend into dead leaves and bark. In Florida, it is found in hammocks, forests, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, and other wooded or semi-wooded habitats where suitable host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on woody plants and contribute to the food web as prey for birds, bats, spiders, and other insect-eating animals.
